ev.q: During 1996--1999, a total of 29,761 fall-related TBI hospitalizations were reported
Compared with persons aged 0--64 years, the rate ratio of hospitalizations was 3.1 for persons aged 65--74 years
Incidence rates were calculated per 100,000 population by using mid-year population estimates
the nonfatal fall-related TBI hospitalization rate was 21.1 per 100,000 population
Among persons aged > 65 years, 60% of falls were on the same level.
Among persons aged > 65 years, the number discharged was 4,927 (41%).
Overall, the nonfatal fall-related TBI hospitalization rate was 21.1 per 100,000 population
Compared with persons aged 0--64 years, the rate ratio of hospitalizations was 3.1 for persons aged 65--74 years
Hospitalization rates increased with age; the highest rate (223.0) was among persons aged > 85 years.
As part of CDC's program of state-based TBI surveillance, California hospital discharge data were collected and analyzed to describe fall-related TBIs.

methods_quotes.q: Incidence rates were calculated per 100,000 population by using mid-year population estimates of California residents for each year
TBI cases were defined by the most recent CDC surveillance definition
Hospitalization records of transfers, fatal cases, and out-of-state residents were excluded by matching sex, date of birth, and a record linkage number
